title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 227 (Principal how far bound, when agent exceeds authority)

content.overview: Section 227 provides that when an agent does more than he is authorised to do, and the part within authority can be separated from the part beyond authority, so much only as is within authority is binding as between the agent and the principal.
content.glance: Separable excess of authority → only the authorised part binds as between agent and principal.
content.study: When an does more than authorised, and the authorised part can be separated from the excess, only the authorised part is binding as between agent and principal. Illustration: A, owner of a ship and cargo, authorises B to procure insurance for 4,000 rupees on the ship; B procures a policy for 4,000 rupees on the ship and another for the like sum on the cargo; A is bound to pay the premium for the ship policy, but not for the cargo policy. Contrast s. 228 (inseparable excess — principal not bound to recognise the transaction).

sections.heading: Excess of authority
sections.body: The agent does more than he is authorised to do.

sections.heading: Separability
sections.body: The part within authority can be separated from the part beyond authority.

sections.heading: Only authorised part binds
sections.body: So much only as is within authority is binding as between the agent and the principal.

provisions.title: Principal how far bound, when agent exceeds authority

examples.title: Statutory illustration — ship and cargo insurance
examples.body: A authorises B to insure the ship for 4,000 rupees. B also insures the cargo for 4,000 rupees. A is bound only for the ship premium, not the cargo premium.

hypotheticals.question: If the excess cannot be separated, does s. 227 apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Inseparable excess is governed by s. 228 — the principal is not bound to recognise the transaction.

distinctions.title: Separable excess (s. 227) vs inseparable excess (s. 228)
distinctions.right: Principal not bound to recognise the transaction

misconceptions.trap: Any excess by the agent binds the principal to the whole deal.
misconceptions.correction: Where the excess is separable, only the authorised part binds under s. 227.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 227 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify excess. II. Test separability. III. If separable, only authorised part binds. IV. Distinguish s. 228 if inseparable. V. Conclude.

examTips: Always pair with s. 228 on inseparability.

illustrations.body: A, being owner of a ship and cargo, authorizes B to procure an insurance for 4,000 rupees on the ship. B procures a policy for 4,000 rupees on the ship, and another for the like sum on the cargo. A is bound to pay the premium for the policy on the ship, but not the premium for the policy on the cargo.
